frameworks.name: Sales Discovery Framework
frameworks.definition: Three-stage sales structure (intro frame + discovery + pitch) where discovery surfaces pain points via questioning, pitch matches those points to solutions, and closing follows naturally from problem-solution alignment.

frameworks.name: Sales Training As Reinforcement Loop
frameworks.definition: Sales competence is built through daily script reinforcement and correct-execution feedback, not hiring for natural talent; most businesses do not know how to train sales.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi's agency, which serves real estate agents, is bottlenecked on sales leadership: he and his COO personally close 20 hours per week in external-growth meetings and are capped at roughly $5M annual new revenue between them, constraining the business from $18M to $100M revenue growth.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Service-based agency selling to real estate agents
claims.mechanism: Founder dependency on personal closing authority masks the true scaling constraint: the sales process is built on founder credibility and expertise, not on replicable discovery + questioning architecture.

numbers.axis: Founder time allocation to sales closing per week

anchors.region: Founder + COO annual new revenue capacity

bounded_by: Applies to consultative, expertise-driven service sales
Does not apply to self-serve SaaS or product-led growth

claims.text: The founder-driven sales process typically relies on consultative expertise and heavy industry knowledge, which is not scalable because it requires the founder/top seller to close; scalable sales processes are prospect-driven (questions + discovery), not salesman-driven (authority + expertise).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: B2B service sales with 15+ minute discovery calls
Selling to business owners with decision authority
claims.mechanism: Founder-driven sales rely on the salesman demonstrating expertise; prospect-driven sales rely on the prospect answering questions and reaching their own conclusion. The second model is trainable across any sales rep; the first requires hiring expensive experts.
bounded_by: Does not apply to transactional one-click sales
Does not apply to high-volume low-price consumer sales

claims.text: A scalable sales script should deliver the absolute minimum amount of information needed for a prospect to make a purchasing decision; overly long scripts force salespeople to demonstrate expertise, which undermines replaceability.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Long scripts compound dependency on the founder's depth of knowledge; shorter scripts force the salesman into a question-based discovery role where they cannot accidentally skip steps or ad-lib authority.
bounded_by: Does not apply to complex enterprise deals requiring extensive customization

claims.text: When a founder personally closes 80%+ of external-growth sales, stopping commission payments on deals the founder helps close will quickly reduce demand for founder involvement in those sales.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales team is asking the founder to close deals
claims.mechanism: Reps who receive full commission regardless of founder involvement have no incentive to close independently; removing the commission when the founder helps removes the incentive to request founder participation.

claims.text: The founder's identity must shift from 'sales god' (executing sales) to 'sales training god' (systematizing sales), and each personal sale should be framed internally as a failure rather than a success because it indicates the systems are not yet replicable.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Founder is the bottleneck on growth
claims.mechanism: Reframing founder closes as failures creates psychological pressure to systematize; it reorients the founder's effort from short-term revenue to long-term leverage.

claims.text: Scalable sales training requires daily reinforcement cadence; 97% of businesses do not know how to train sales, instead hiring and seeing who sticks; if the script is successful, the role is 100% trainable through repetition and feedback.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales role with documented, repeatable script
claims.mechanism: Script execution is a learned behavior, trainable via reinforcement (repetition + feedback); most managers do not invest in daily training because they confuse hiring for natural talent with systematic training.

numbers.axis: Percentage of businesses that know how to train sales

anchors.region: Businesses that know how to systematically train sales

bounded_by: Requires a proven, successful script in place before training begins

claims.text: The correct phone pitch for complex service sales should surface the prospect's pain points without providing detailed product/solution information. The pitch statement should be: 'You said you have [pain]. We solve that. The people who help with that are really good. Do you want to do it or not?' This frames the prospect as the hero, not the salesman.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: B2B service sales with business owner decision-maker
claims.mechanism: Detailed product explanations position the salesman as the expert/hero; minimal pitch language forces the prospect to own the decision, increasing close likelihood. The salesman becomes a facilitator, not an authority figure.
bounded_by: Does not apply to product-based or feature-driven sales

claims.text: Sales questions should be designed to uncover pain points; solution details should only be provided after pain is acknowledged, and in the form of matching problem-to-solution pairs, not as feature lists.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Prospects resist solutions when presented before they acknowledge a problem; surfacing the problem first makes the solution appear logical rather than salesy.

claims.text: A founder's direct involvement in closing undermines the replicated sales team by positioning the founder as the subject-matter expert; when the founder comes in, they implicitly communicate 'you need me to understand this,' which signals that the younger/less-experienced rep is not equipped to solve the prospect's problem.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Founder is significantly more experienced than the sales team
claims.mechanism: Founder involvement is a credibility signal; it communicates to the prospect that the rep alone is insufficient, undermining the rep's ability to close similar deals independently in the future.

examples.text: Alex describes his agency's real estate service business: $17-18M annual revenue, founders doing 20 hours/week in closing meetings, wanting to reach $100M. The leads are flowing (not the constraint), but sales leadership bottleneck is severe. The founder explains that regardless of what he does to step back, the sales team and prospects still request his presence in close meetings.

Alex contrasts the two sales process models: his consultative model (where he, as the founder, brings deep real estate industry knowledge and authority to close high-value deals) versus a scalable prospect-driven model (where a 22-year-old rep with no authority uses structured questions to guide the prospect to a self-owned decision). He notes that the consultative approach feels natural to him but scales poorly because it requires hiring expensive experts or has the founder do all closing.

Alex describes the typical hiring fallacy: a business owner hires 10 salespeople, fires the ones who don't stick, and calls the remaining ones 'naturals.' If that business owner instead had a systematic training cadence (daily scripting + feedback + reinforcement), they could take almost any hire and turn them into a closer by teaching them to execute the script correctly.

practices.text: Do not pay commissions on sales that the founder helps close; this removes the rep's financial incentive to ask the founder to participate and forces them to develop independent closing ability.
Implement daily sales training cadence (daily huddles + script reinforcement) rather than assuming hires are naturals; treat each salesman's adherence to script as the success metric.
Cut script length by half or more; remove product details and leave only the minimum information (pain + solution match + call-to-action) needed for a prospect to make a buying decision.
Reframe founder involvement in closing: each founder close should be internally noted as a process failure (systemization gap) rather than a sales success.
